question: Should OpenClaw ship this deny-over-allow exec policy as a full native config/protocol/runtime contract, or narrow the first version before merge?
rationale: The PR changes a host-command security boundary and adds persisted config/API surface; automation can identify wiring defects, but maintainers should confirm the intended policy scope and prompt-versus-deny semantics before landing it.

options.title: Complete the native contract
options.body: Require the PR to wire the denylist through config validation, protocol writes, gateway and node hosts, and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the first version
options.body: Accept only a smaller exec-approvals-file or gateway-only contract after updating docs/tests/proof to make unsupported paths explicit.

options.title: Pause for policy design
options.body: Hold or close this implementation if maintainers want to settle broader exec denylist, path-deny, and UI/API direction first.

recommendation.title: Complete the native contract
recommendation.body: Require the PR to wire the denylist through config validation, protocol writes, gateway and node hosts, and real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current signal across the prior issue review, exec approvals security policy, and adjacent gateway/node documentation history.
